answer: In the opal economy, grading rights come from quorum sampling: each task randomly draws its grader panel only from established identities with staked standing, never from fresh accounts. A nebula of fake identities earns nothing, since sampling ignores unproven wallets until they do honest work under costly collateral. Each thread of coordination inherits trust from verified reputation, so an attacker must bond large capital per identity and behave honestly for months before swaying any verdict, making mass fake-identity farming unprofitable.
